amgen-scholars-europe-karolinska-2027.about:
Amgen Scholars Europe gives undergraduates a funded summer of hands-on research in a lab at one of five leading European institutions (ETH Zurich, Institut Pasteur, Karolinska Institutet, LMU Munich and the University of Cambridge). Scholars work on a real research project, attend seminars on science and drug discovery, and in early September everyone meets at the Amgen Scholars Europe Symposium at the University of Cambridge (travel, room and board for the symposium are covered).

You do not need to study at the host: you must be enrolled at a university in a country of the European Higher Education Area (Bologna Process), which includes Georgia, Türkiye, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Ukraine and the whole EU. Each host runs its own application and its own support package for housing, meals and travel; you may apply to several hosts.
highlights: Real research project in a top European lab
Open to students at universities in all Bologna Process countries, including Georgia
Symposium at Cambridge with travel, room and board covered
amgen-scholars-europe-karolinska-2027.eligibility: Undergraduates enrolled at a university in a European Higher Education Area (Bologna Process) country, including Georgia, in the second year of a three-year bachelor's or the second/third year of a four-year integrated programme at the time of application. Strong academic record and interest in a PhD. Nationality is not restricted.
how_to_apply: Choose one or more hosts and open each host's Amgen Scholars page (linked from amgenscholars.com/europe-programme)
Prepare an official transcript, a personal statement and a recommendation letter
Submit a separate application to each host by 1 February 2027
Selected scholars are notified in spring and must attend the Cambridge symposium in September
amgen-scholars-europe-karolinska-2027.costs: Housing, meals and travel support for the summer vary by host (see the host's page); the September symposium in Cambridge is fully covered. No tuition.

amlmun-2026.about:
AML MUN is a student-led conference hosted by Anavryta Model Lyceum in Marousi (Athens). The 5th edition expects about 350 delegates in 10 committees under the theme 'Countdown to 2030: measuring progress, holding accountability and finalising policies on SDGs'.

The conference runs 27–29 November 2026 at Anavryta Model Lyceum, Kifisias Avenue 184, Marousi, Athens, Greece. It is open to secondary school students registered through their schools. Working language: English.

Schools register their delegations through 'Register (SCHOOLS)' on the official site; staff/press applications are also open. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: 10 committees incl. Security Council and Historical Crisis
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
amlmun-2026.eligibility: Open to secondary school students registered through their schools. Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Schools register their delegations through 'Register (SCHOOLS)' on the official site; staff/press applications are also open.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
amlmun-2026.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

ammun-2026.about:
AMMUN (Amman Model United Nations) was founded in 2002 by students of the Amman Baccalaureate School and has grown into a THIMUN-affiliated conference of international standing. The conference runs on 18–22 November 2026 at the Grand Hyatt Hotel in Amman.

Schools register delegations through an online form (number of students and supervisors, student-officer applications) and can join an excursion to Petra. Delegates debate in General Assemblies, ECOSOC and other THIMUN-style forums.

A well-established THIMUN conference and a good reason to visit Jordan.
highlights: Held at the Grand Hyatt Amman
ammun-2026.eligibility: Secondary-school students attending with their school delegation and supervisors. English is the working language.
how_to_apply: Read About and Schedule on ammun.abs.edu.jo
School MUN director fills in the Registration form
Apply for student-officer roles if desired
Attend 18–22 November 2026
ammun-2026.costs: Fees are communicated to schools after registration; hotel and travel extra.

amstermun-2026.about:
AmsterMUN, founded in 2025 as Amsterdam's first independent MUN, returns for its 2026 edition with about 250 expected delegates, 20+ chairs and 10 committees including the African Union, UNODC, UNHCR, European Council, Interpol, ILO, a League of Nations and a Security Council.

The conference runs 20–22 November 2026 at venues in Amsterdam, Netherlands. It is open to high school and university students from across Europe and beyond. Working language: English.

Apply through the 'Apply Now' button on the official site; the FAQ explains delegation and payment details. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: 10 committees incl. African Union, Interpol and a League of Nations
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
amstermun-2026.eligibility: Open to high school and university students from across Europe and beyond. Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.

Apply through the 'Apply Now' button on the official site; the FAQ explains delegation and payment details.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.

amstermun-2026.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

app-academy-open.about:
App Academy Open is the free, self-paced version of App Academy's software engineering bootcamp curriculum. It includes lessons, exercises and projects across JavaScript, Python, SQL, React and full-stack development.

It is designed for people who want bootcamp-level material without paying tuition; learners can later choose to apply for App Academy's paid, instructor-led programmes if they want more support.

Sign-up is free on the App Academy website.
highlights: Option to move to an instructor-led programme later
how_to_apply: Open the App Academy Open page.
Create a free account.
Work through the curriculum at your own pace.
Build the portfolio projects.
app-academy-open.costs: Free (paid bootcamps are separate and optional).

assist-scholars-2027-28.about:
ASSIST is a non-profit that places international secondary students for a full academic year at member U.S. independent (mostly boarding) schools. The premier Sanderson Scholarship covers tuition, room and board for one year, valued up to US$84,000; the student pays about US$20,000 for the programme fee, flights, visa and mandatory U.S. health insurance, and donor-funded reductions of up to 80% are possible based on need. Fully funded places are rare and very competitive.

Applicants are 14-18, typically entering grade 10 or 11, with high English proficiency and university plans. Local offices exist in Austria, Bulgaria, Colombia, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, Georgia, Germany, Hungary, Lithuania, Moldova, Norway, Poland, Serbia, Slovakia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and Türkiye; students elsewhere use the 'All Other Countries' route.

The application (form, transcripts, three teacher recommendations, parent statement, photos, short video) opens in July; full application due 1 December (Germany/Switzerland part by 15 November). Interviews run in December-January, decisions in January-February and school placements in March-April.
highlights: Scholarship worth up to US$84,000 at a U.S. boarding school
Georgia has an ASSIST country office; any country can apply
Need-based reductions of up to 80% on the remaining fee
assist-scholars-2027-28.eligibility: Non-U.S. students aged 14-18, typically entering grade 10 or 11 (limited 12th-grade/postgraduate places), with high English proficiency (Duolingo test may be required), planning university study, committing to a full 10-month year and returning home.
how_to_apply: Start the online application (opens each July)
Submit form, transcripts, 3 teacher recommendations, parent statement, photos and intro video by 1 Dec 2026
Take the Duolingo English Test if asked (by 15 Dec)
Interview in Dec-Jan
Decision in Jan-Feb; school placement in Mar-Apr
assist-scholars-2027-28.costs: Scholarship covers tuition, room and board (up to US$84,000). Family pays about US$20,000 (programme fee, travel, visa, insurance); up to 80% reduction possible on need.

astro-pi-mission-space-lab-2026-27.about:
Mission Space Lab teams of 2–6 young people, supervised by a mentor, write and test a Python program that uses the Astro Pi's camera and sensors on the ISS to complete a scientific task set by ESA (recent editions asked teams to calculate the speed of the ISS). Programs that pass testing are run in orbit and teams receive their data and a certificate.

It is a genuine taste of space-mission software engineering and an excellent project for applications in engineering and physics.
astro-pi-mission-space-lab-2026-27.eligibility: Age 19 or under, in teams of 2–6 with a mentor, at schools/clubs in ESA Member States or Canada, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia; at least 50% of team members nationals of these countries.
how_to_apply: A mentor registers the team on astro-pi.org by 22 Feb 2027
Follow the project guide and write the program
Test with the Astro Pi emulator
Mentor submits the program before the deadline

astro-pi-mission-zero-2026-27.about:
In Mission Zero, participants (alone or in teams of up to four) write a program that reads a sensor on the Astro Pi computer on the ISS and uses it to set the background colour of a pixel image for the astronauts. It takes about an hour, needs no prior coding experience, and every valid program runs in space; participants receive a certificate showing where the ISS was when their code ran.

A mentor (teacher, parent, club leader) registers and gets a classroom code. Eligibility is limited to ESA member states and partner countries.
highlights: Your code runs on the ISS
astro-pi-mission-zero-2026-27.eligibility: Age 19 or under, supervised by a mentor, enrolled in a school or club in an ESA Member State (Austria, Belgium, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, UK) or Canada, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia; at least 50% of each team must be nationals of these countries.
how_to_apply: A mentor registers on astro-pi.org and gets a classroom code
Follow the step-by-step Mission Zero guide
Write and test your Python program in the online emulator
Submit before 22 March 2027, 12:00 CET

atlassian-codegeist-2026.about:
Codegeist is Atlassian's annual developer hackathon. Entrants build a new app (or rebuild an existing one) on Atlassian Forge that integrates with at least one Atlassian product or capability, then submit a demo video, description and code on the hackathon site.

Judging runs 5 January–3 February 2027 and winners are announced around 15 February 2027. It is fully online, so university students anywhere (subject to the rules' country exclusions) can take part and build a portfolio project around widely used developer tools.
highlights: Build on Atlassian Forge (Jira, Confluence, Rovo)
atlassian-codegeist-2026.eligibility: Individuals who are at least the age of majority where they live (usually 18+), teams of eligible individuals, and organisations. Standard Devpost exclusions apply (residents of US-embargoed countries/regions and certain other jurisdictions; sponsor employees). Check the official rules before entering.
how_to_apply: Register on codegeist2026.devpost.com
Set up a free Atlassian developer account and Forge CLI
Build and test your Forge app
Submit video, description and repo before 22 Dec 2026, 12:00 pm PT

aubmunc-2027.about:
AUBMUNC is the official Model United Nations conference of the American University of Beirut and has run for nearly ten years. The 2027 edition (its 10th) combines pre-conference training and preparation resources, an on-campus mock conference, and the final conference on Saturday–Sunday 10–11 April 2027 in West Hall, AUB.

Schools register delegations through an advisor, and students can also register as independent delegates. No prior MUN experience is required; committees cover political, humanitarian, economic, legal and environmental topics, all in English. Outstanding delegates may be recognised with awards and, subject to availability, scholarships and internship opportunities offered through AUBMUNC partners.

A strong choice for school students in Lebanon and the region who want a university-level conference on one of the Middle East's best-known campuses.
highlights: Hosted at the American University of Beirut
Training programme plus mock conference before the final event
aubmunc-2027.eligibility: School students registering through their school (advisor) or as independent delegates. English is the official language of all committees.
how_to_apply: Read the announcement and conference page on mun.org.lb
Advisors register the school delegation by 23 Nov 2026 (or register as an independent delegate)
Attend the training sessions and mock conference
Take part in the final conference at AUB on 10–11 April 2027
aubmunc-2027.costs: Fees are provided on registration through the official portal; travel and accommodation extra.

awesomemath-summer-program-2027.about:
AwesomeMath, founded by olympiad coach Titu Andreescu, runs an intensive online summer programme in problem solving: number theory, algebra, combinatorics and geometry courses at four levels, taught live Monday to Friday by an international faculty. In 2026 there were three sessions (8–26 June, 29 June – 17 July, 20 July – 7 August).

Admission is by an entrance test (Part I for levels 1–2, Part II for levels 3–4). It is a good preparation path for national olympiads and AMC/AIME-style competitions and is open to students worldwide.
highlights: Olympiad-style courses at four levels taught by experienced coaches
Three online sessions to choose from
awesomemath-summer-program-2027.eligibility: Middle- and high-school students roughly 12–18 years old, from any country, who pass the admission test.
how_to_apply: Check the AwesomeMath site in mid-December 2026 for 2027 enrolment
Take the admission test (choose Part I or II according to your level)
Submit the application by the early deadline (mid-January) for the best price, or by later rounds
Choose your session and courses after admission
awesomemath-summer-program-2027.costs: Tuition varies by session and application round (see the site); each course includes a free book. Online, so no travel or housing costs.

awmun-xvii-2027.about:
Asia World Model United Nations (AWMUN) is a series of international conferences run by International Global Network, the organiser of AYIMUN. The 17th edition takes place in Seoul, South Korea, on 8–12 April 2027, with committee sessions, cultural programme and awards.

High-school and university students from around the world can register as delegates or observers through the official site.

A five-day international MUN in Seoul for students who want to combine debate with travel in Korea.
awmun-xvii-2027.eligibility: High-school and university students worldwide. English is the working language.
how_to_apply: Open modelunitednation.org and choose AWMUN XVII Seoul
Register as a delegate or observer
Pay through the payment portal after acceptance
Attend 8–12 April 2027
awmun-xvii-2027.costs: Fees and packages shown on the official site; travel and visas extra.

aws-restart-cloud-careers.about:
AWS re/Start is Amazon Web Services' workforce programme for people starting a cloud career. Cohorts are run with collaborating organisations in many countries and combine instructor-led sessions, hands-on labs (Linux, Python, networking, security, AWS services) and job-interview coaching.

It targets adults (18+) who are unemployed or underemployed; no previous IT experience is needed. Participants get free practice and full AWS Certification exam vouchers and connections to employers.

You apply through the country-specific site of the local collaborating organisation; requirements and cohort dates vary by location.
aws-restart-cloud-careers.eligibility: Adults 18+ who are unemployed or underemployed and can attend the sessions; country-specific requirements apply.
how_to_apply: Open the AWS re/Start page and choose your country.
Contact the local collaborating organisation via its site.
Complete their application and assessment.
Join the next cohort start date.
aws-restart-cloud-careers.costs: Free to learners, including certification exam vouchers.

ayimun-24-2027.about:
AYIMUN (Asia Youth International Model United Nations) is a recurring international conference organised by International Global Network. Its 24th edition takes place in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, on 15–18 January 2027, bringing together delegates from many countries for committee sessions, cultural activities and awards.

School and university students can register as delegates or observers; the organiser publishes official delegate lists and a payment portal on its site.

An accessible international MUN for students in Asia who want to meet peers from many countries.
highlights: International delegates; delegate and observer roles
ayimun-24-2027.eligibility: High-school and university students worldwide. English is the working language.

Complete the delegate registration form
Wait for acceptance and pay via the payment portal
Attend 15–18 January 2027
ayimun-24-2027.costs: Registration and package fees shown on the official site after selection; flights and visas extra.

bcimun-2027.about:
BCIMUN is the first session of a new student-run international MUN at Byron College in Athens, themed 'Shared Challenges, Shared Accountability'.

The conference runs 16–18 April 2027 at the Byron College campus, Leoforos Anthousas 46, Athens, Greece. It is open to students aged 13–18, normally in school delegations. Working language: English.

Schools apply via 'Applications (School Delegations)'; student officers apply via the separate form on the official site. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: Inaugural edition: easier to get chair/officer roles
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page

Schools apply via 'Applications (School Delegations)'; student officers apply via the separate form on the official site.

bcmun-2026.about:
BCMUN is an international MUN held in a resort hotel in Antalya, Türkiye, with committees such as the International Labour Organization.

The conference runs 3–6 December 2026 at a resort hotel in Antalya, Türkiye. It is open to high school and university students from any country. Working language: English.

Apply through 'Apply Now!' on the official site. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Packages usually include hotel accommodation. The Hungarian edition runs in five age categories; teachers register on the e-hod admin site.

Bebras tasks are short, interactive puzzles that build computational thinking — algorithms, patterns and data — without requiring programming knowledge. Students in different age groups take a timed challenge online under teacher supervision.

Try the practice challenges
Take the challenge in class 9–20 Nov 2026

bennington-young-writers-awards-2027.about:
The Bennington Young Writers Awards recognise outstanding writing by students in grades 9–12. Each student may enter one category: fiction (one story or excerpt), nonfiction (one personal or creative essay) or poetry (1–3 poems), each up to 1,500 words. Entries must be in English and approved by a sponsoring teacher or, for homeschoolers, a mentor.

Prizes: $2,000, $1,000 and $500 plus $250 for distinguished entries; winners who enrol at Bennington receive full-tuition (first place) or half-tuition scholarships, and finalists $25,000 a year. Grade-12 entrants must first submit a Common App or Coalition application indicating interest. AI-assisted entries are disqualified.
highlights: Full-tuition Bennington scholarship for first place
bennington-young-writers-awards-2027.eligibility: Students in grades 9–12 anywhere in the world, writing in English, sponsored by a teacher or mentor; one entry per student; seniors must have started a Common App/Coalition application.
how_to_apply: Choose fiction, nonfiction or poetry (max 1,500 words)
Get a sponsoring teacher's approval
Submit online before 1 November, 11:59 pm ET

berkeley-skydeck-batch-24-2027.about:
Berkeley SkyDeck is the University of California, Berkeley's startup accelerator. Every six months it admits around 20 Cohort startups, which receive roughly US$210,000 in investment from the Berkeley SkyDeck Fund, plus Pad-13 teams that get the same space, mentors and network without guaranteed investment.

The programme runs about six months in Berkeley, California, with hundreds of advisors, industry partners and a Demo Day for investors. Startups from all over the world are eligible and encouraged; UC-affiliated and international teams are a stated priority.

Batch 24 applications open in January 2027 on the SkyDeck site. It suits student and graduate founders with a working product or strong prototype who can relocate to the Bay Area for the programme.
highlights: About US$210,000 investment for Cohort startups
Open to founders worldwide; international teams prioritised
Mentors, UC Berkeley network and investor Demo Day
berkeley-skydeck-batch-24-2027.eligibility: Startups from any country; at least one founder should be able to work from Berkeley during the programme. UC affiliation is a plus but not required.
how_to_apply: Check the SkyDeck apply page in January 2027 for the Batch 24 window.
Prepare a pitch deck, team details and traction.
Submit the online application.
Interview with the SkyDeck team if shortlisted.
berkeley-skydeck-batch-24-2027.costs: No fee. Cohort track: about US$210,000 investment from the Berkeley SkyDeck Fund (equity). Living and travel costs are the founders' own.

berlin-house-of-representatives-grant-pr.about:
The Grant Programme of the Foundation of the Berlin House of Representatives brings outstanding young researchers in any subject to Berlin for almost a full year. It is open to applicants from the United States, the United Kingdom, France and the successor states of the Soviet Union, which includes Georgia. Projects should concern Berlin, German issues or Germany's international relations, or require access to Berlin's research institutions.

About 15 grants are awarded each year for 10 months: €1,100 per month for pre-doctoral students and €1,630 per month for post-doctoral researchers, plus a fixed travel allowance (€200 within Europe, €600 from outside Europe). Grant holders take part in Berlin's academic life and get to know the city's culture and people.

Candidates need at least a first degree, a detailed research plan and a written commitment from a Berlin professor or research-institute director to supervise them. Researchers should be no older than 35 and students generally no older than 25. The deadline is 15 December each year.
highlights: Ten months in Berlin with a monthly grant
Explicitly open to researchers from Georgia and other post-Soviet states
Small cohort (~15) gives real access to Berlin institutions
berlin-house-of-representatives-grant-pr.eligibility: Young researchers of excellent academic merit from the US, UK, France or a post-Soviet state (incl. Georgia); at least a first degree; researchers max. 35, students generally max. 25; research on Berlin/German topics or needing Berlin institutions; confirmed Berlin supervisor.
how_to_apply: Secure a supervision commitment from a professor or institute director in Berlin
Write a detailed research plan
Download the application forms from the Foundation's page linked in the DAAD database
Submit by 15 December 2026
berlin-house-of-representatives-grant-pr.costs: Grant: €1,100/month (pre-doctoral) or €1,630/month (post-doctoral) for 10 months plus €200–600 travel allowance.

The Austrian edition is run in German by the Austrian Computer Society (OCG).

biber-der-informatik-austria-2026.costs: Free (some national organisers may charge a small school fee).

biohacks-2026.about:
BioHacks 2026 is a two-day biomedical case challenge where students from health sciences, engineering and business pick a track, build a solution and pitch it to judges. It is an official Major League Hacking (MLH) 2027-season member event, held in person at McMaster University in Hamilton from 2026-11-07 to 2026-11-08. Participants form small teams (typically up to four; check the event rules), attend workshops and talks, and present a working prototype to judges at the end.

Food, workspace, Wi-Fi, swag and mentoring are provided free of charge. Beginners are welcome: MLH events run introductory workshops and expect many first-time hackers. Applications are handled on the event's own website; spots are limited and usually confirmed a few weeks before the event.

Hackathons are one of the fastest ways to build a portfolio project, meet engineers from sponsoring companies and practise teamwork under time pressure.
highlights: Build a portfolio project in one weekend
biohacks-2026.eligibility: Students (see the event FAQ for high-school and university eligibility).
how_to_apply: Open https://www.bioeng4youth.ca/ and sign up for application updates or apply if the form is open
Form a small team or join one at the event
Complete the application and accept the MLH Code of Conduct
Confirm your spot when accepted and arrange your own travel unless reimbursement is offered
Attend in person and submit your project for judging
biohacks-2026.costs: Free to attend; meals, snacks and workspace provided. Travel and accommodation are usually at your own cost unless the event announces travel reimbursement.

biozentrum-research-summer-2027.about:
The Biozentrum Research Summer lets undergraduate students join a research group at the University of Basel's Biozentrum, a leading centre for molecular and biomedical research (structural biology, cell biology, neurobiology, infection biology, computational biology). The working language is English, and the internship ends with a written report on the research results.

Participants receive a time-proportional stipend of CHF 1,736 per month (gross) and a participation certificate. It is open only to Swiss or EU citizens and Swiss C-permit holders; an EU residence permit alone does not qualify.
highlights: Research in one of Europe's top molecular-biology institutes
biozentrum-research-summer-2027.eligibility: Undergraduates in life sciences and related sciences who hold Swiss or EU citizenship or a Swiss C-permit. Not open to other nationalities.
how_to_apply: Prepare a one-page motivation letter, CV and transcripts
Open the application platform between 4 January and 28 February 2027
Submit the form with all documents before 12:00 noon CET on 28 February
biozentrum-research-summer-2027.costs: Stipend CHF 1,736 per month (gross), time-proportional. Housing not provided.

bird-photographer-of-the-year-youth-2027.about:
Bird Photographer of the Year celebrates the world's best bird photography while supporting bird conservation. The youth competition has three age groups (11 and under, 12–14, 15–17); young photographers may submit up to 10 images for free.

Winning and commended images appear in the annual book and exhibition, and winners are announced in September 2027. High-resolution files are requested from shortlisted entrants in February 2027.
bird-photographer-of-the-year-youth-2027.eligibility: Photographers aged 17 and under, anywhere in the world; parental consent required.
how_to_apply: Read the rules and youth categories on birdpoty.com
Create an account on the entry portal
Upload up to 10 bird photos before 13 Dec 2026

birdmun-2027.about:
BirdMUN is the one-day Model UN conference of Keene High School in New Hampshire, with a guest speaker and several committees.

The conference runs 6 March 2027 at Keene High School, New Hampshire, United States. It is open to high school delegations. Working language: English.

Bring your delegation via 'Register now!' on the official site. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
birdmun-2027.eligibility: Open to high school delegations. Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Bring your delegation via 'Register now!' on the official site.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
birdmun-2027.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

bkmun-2-2026.about:
BKMUN 2.0 is the student-run Model United Nations conference of Beaconhouse College Programme (BCP), Karakoram campus. Its second edition runs on 27–29 November 2026 at the campus, with twelve committees and forums spanning general assemblies, crisis and specialised bodies.

It is aimed at school and college students who want three days of debate, negotiation and resolution writing, and offers dais (chair) applications and a student ambassador programme as well as delegate places.

A compact, school-friendly conference for students in Islamabad and northern Pakistan, and a good step up after a first MUN.
bkmun-2-2026.eligibility: School and college students (mainly O/A-level and intermediate). English is the working language.
how_to_apply: Visit bkmun.xyz and read the committees
Click Register now and complete the delegate form
Pay the delegate fee as instructed
Prepare your position paper and attend 27–29 November
bkmun-2-2026.costs: Delegate fee is shown during registration on the official site; travel and accommodation are not included.

bocconi-summer-school-bachelor-students-.about:
Bocconi's Summer School for Bachelor Students is a three-week intensive programme in Milan for undergraduates from Italian and non-Italian universities (Bocconi's own students cannot apply). Each course has 48 hours of teaching, normally on weekday mornings, plus company visits, assignments and extracurricular activities. Students who sit the final exam on campus earn 6 ECTS credits; everyone who meets attendance gets a digital certificate.

In 2026 the programme ran 29 June – 17 July and courses covered management, finance, law, AI and sustainability. Applications are made through Bocconi's My Application portal with a recent transcript, and the place is secured by paying the fee; popular courses fill quickly.
highlights: Earn 6 ECTS credits with an on-campus final exam
Company visits and an international cohort in Milan
bocconi-summer-school-bachelor-students-.eligibility: Students currently enrolled in a bachelor's programme at any university other than Bocconi, from any country. Courses taught in English.
how_to_apply: Check the Bocconi Summer School page for the 2027 course list and timeline
Apply on the My Application portal with your latest transcript (or certificate of enrolment) in English
Select your course and pay the fee to secure the place
Sit the final exam on the last day if you want 6 ECTS credits
bocconi-summer-school-bachelor-students-.costs: 2026 participation fee EUR 2,700 (reduced fee EUR 2,500 for eligible categories). Accommodation, meals and travel not included.

bocconi-summer-school-high-school-2027.about:
The Bocconi Summer School for High School Students is a short on-campus programme at one of Europe's top business and economics universities in Milan. Students choose labs in fields such as economics, management, finance, law, AI and sustainability, attend morning lectures by Bocconi faculty, work on a group project presented on the last day, and hear guest speakers from industry. In 2026 it ran 6–17 July (one- or two-week options), with an extra law lab taught in Italian.

It is open to students in Italy or abroad in their third-to-last or second-to-last year of high school who are at least 15 at the start. Places are allocated in order of completed (paid) applications and the 2026 edition sold out early, so apply as soon as the 2027 call opens.
highlights: Labs taught by Bocconi faculty in economics, management, law and AI
Group project and guest speakers from industry
Milan campus experience; optional on-campus housing
bocconi-summer-school-high-school-2027.eligibility: High-school students in their third-to-last or second-to-last year (Italy or abroad), aged 15+ by the programme start. All nationalities. Classes in English (one law lab in Italian).
how_to_apply: Watch the Bocconi Summer School page for the 2027 call
Register on the My Application portal
Upload ID/passport (yours and a parent's), photo and school transcripts in English or Italian
Choose 2 preferred labs and pay the programme fee to secure your spot
Apply early: places are first-come, first-served
bocconi-summer-school-high-school-2027.costs: 2026 participation fee EUR 2,700 (two weeks); optional accommodation about EUR 1,600 for two weeks; meals and travel extra. Refund only for force majeure (EUR 350 retained).

bosmun-xxvi-2027.about:
BosMUN is Boston University's award-winning high-school Model UN, organised by the BU International Affairs Association and now in its 26th session.

The conference runs 5–7 February 2027 at the Marriott Copley and Boston Sheraton hotels, United States. It is open to high school students and school delegations. Working language: English.

Use 'Register Now' on the official site. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: Run by Boston University's International Affairs Association
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
bosmun-xxvi-2027.eligibility: Open to high school students and school delegations. Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Use 'Register Now' on the official site.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
bosmun-xxvi-2027.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

bostonhacks-2026.about:
BostonHacks 2026 is Boston University's hackathon, themed 'Boston Bound' this year. It is an official Major League Hacking (MLH) 2027-season member event, held in person at Boston University in Boston from 2026-11-21 to 2026-11-22. Participants form small teams (typically up to four; check the event rules), attend workshops and talks, and present a working prototype to judges at the end.

Food, workspace, Wi-Fi, swag and mentoring are provided free of charge. Beginners are welcome: MLH events run introductory workshops and expect many first-time hackers. Applications are handled on the event's own website; spots are limited and usually confirmed a few weeks before the event.

Hackathons are one of the fastest ways to build a portfolio project, meet engineers from sponsoring companies and practise teamwork under time pressure.
highlights: Build a portfolio project in one weekend
bostonhacks-2026.eligibility: Students enrolled at a college or university (many MLH events also admit high-school students aged 18+, and some all ages 13+ with consent). Participants must follow the MLH Code of Conduct. International students may attend but must arrange their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open https://bostonhacks.org/ and sign up for application updates or apply if the form is open
Form a small team or join one at the event
Complete the application and accept the MLH Code of Conduct
Confirm your spot when accepted and arrange your own travel unless reimbursement is offered
Attend in person and submit your project for judging
bostonhacks-2026.costs: Free to attend; meals, snacks and workspace provided. Travel and accommodation are usually at your own cost unless the event announces travel reimbursement.

british-informatics-olympiad-2027.about:
The British Informatics Olympiad's first round is a three-hour programming exam taken at school under teacher supervision, in any programming language, with problems that mix coding and logical reasoning. Teachers register on the BIO site and mark papers using the provided scheme.

Top scorers are invited to the final at Churchill College, Cambridge (2026's ran 3–5 April), and the best finalists go on to the training camp that picks the UK team for the International Olympiad in Informatics.
british-informatics-olympiad-2027.eligibility: Full-time students in UK schools (see the BIO information pack for age rules).
how_to_apply: Ask your computing teacher to register with BIO
Sit round one in school during the Dec–Jan window
Await results and a possible final invitation
Attend the Cambridge final in spring
british-informatics-olympiad-2027.costs: Free to enter; the final is funded by sponsors.

british-mathematical-olympiad-2026-27.about:
BMO1 is a 3.5-hour paper of six proof-based problems; BMO2 (by invitation) has four harder problems. Students qualify through high scores in the Senior Mathematical Challenge (held 7 October 2026), and schools can also make a limited number of discretionary entries for strong students.

Top BMO2 performers are invited to the UK IMO training programme.
highlights: Pathway to IMO and EGMO teams
british-mathematical-olympiad-2026-27.eligibility: Students in UK schools who qualify via the Senior Mathematical Challenge or are entered as discretionary candidates by their school.
how_to_apply: Check with your maths teacher whether you qualified from the SMC
Ask about a discretionary entry if you did not
Sit BMO1 in school on 18 Nov 2026
Qualify for BMO2 on 20 Jan 2027
british-mathematical-olympiad-2026-27.costs: Discretionary entries carry a fee; qualifying entries are free or low-cost.

bu-academic-immersion-2027.about:
Academic Immersion (AIM) programmes focus on one subject for three weeks, combining classes with labs, field trips and projects around Boston; recent tracks include topics such as medicine and health, neuroscience, engineering, law and game design. Students live in BU residence halls or commute.

Two sessions in 2027: 27 June – 16 July and 18 July – 6 August. International students can apply through BU's visiting international student process.
highlights: Three-week single-topic immersion with field trips
bu-academic-immersion-2027.eligibility: Rising high-school juniors and seniors, including international students with sufficient English.
how_to_apply: Pick an Academic Immersion track and session
Apply online (application opens in winter)
Submit transcript and supporting documents; international students add English proficiency
Pay the programme fee and arrange travel/visa
bu-academic-immersion-2027.costs: Paid programme fee covering tuition and (for residential students) housing and meals; see the BU site for 2027 amounts.

bu-high-school-honors-2027.about:
High School Honors lets strong high-school students enrol in regular BU summer courses alongside university students, choosing from more than 80 courses across the sciences, engineering, humanities, social sciences and business, and earning transferable college credit with a BU transcript.

The 2027 programme runs 27 June – 6 August in residential, commuter or online formats. International students are welcome (BU has a dedicated 'visiting international students' registration track and visa guidance). Fees include tuition per credit plus housing/dining for residential students.
highlights: Real BU undergraduate courses for college credit
More than 80 courses to choose from
bu-high-school-honors-2027.eligibility: Rising high-school juniors and seniors with a strong academic record, including international students with sufficient English.
how_to_apply: Choose two courses on the BU Summer Term site
Submit the online application with transcript, recommendation and essay
International students: provide English proficiency evidence and arrange an F-1/visa as advised by BU
Pay tuition and housing once admitted
bu-high-school-honors-2027.costs: Paid: BU summer tuition per credit plus residential fees (published on the BU Summer Term site). Limited financial aid may be available.

bundestag-international-parliamentary-sc.about:
The International Parliamentary Scholarship (IPS) is awarded by the German Bundestag together with Berlin's Freie Universität, Humboldt-Universität and Technische Universität. Each year up to 120 young graduates from about 50 participating countries, including Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Moldova and Ukraine, come to Berlin from 1 March to 31 July.

Fellows attend events and seminars and complete a three-month work placement with a Member of the Bundestag, getting first-hand experience of German parliamentary democracy. The programme aims to strengthen democratic values, tolerance and understanding of cultural diversity, and to build ties between participating countries and Germany.

The scholarship is worth €700 per month and includes free accommodation, health, accident and liability insurance, and reimbursed travel to and from Berlin. Candidates need a university degree, a strong interest in politics and good German. Application deadlines differ by country, so check the Georgia entry on the Bundestag IPS page well in advance.
highlights: Three-month placement in a Bundestag member's office
bundestag-international-parliamentary-sc.eligibility: Nationals of a participating country (incl. Georgia); completed university degree; strong interest in politics; good German (see programme rules for age and language requirements).
how_to_apply: Check the Georgia deadline and forms on the Bundestag IPS page
Prepare the application in German with CV, degree and references
Submit by the country deadline; shortlisted candidates are interviewed
bundestag-international-parliamentary-sc.costs: €700/month, free accommodation, insurance and travel reimbursement.

bundestag-ppp-2028-29.about:
The Parlamentarisches Patenschafts-Programm (PPP) has been run since 1983 by the German Bundestag and the U.S. Congress (in the U.S. it is called CBYX). Each year it awards full scholarships to school students and young professionals from Germany to spend a year in the United States: school students live with a host family and attend a high school; young professionals study at a college and do an internship. Each scholar is sponsored by a Member of the Bundestag.

The 44th PPP (2027-28) closed on 11 September 2026. The 45th PPP (2028-29) is expected to open in May 2027; watch bundestag.de/ppp and apply online in that window. AFS Germany and other exchange organisations implement the programme.
highlights: Full Bundestag scholarship for a year in the USA
Sponsored by a Member of Parliament
bundestag-ppp-2028-29.eligibility: School students and young professionals living in Germany (age and nationality rules in the PPP call).
how_to_apply: Watch bundestag.de/ppp for the May 2027 opening
Apply online in the application window
Attend selection interviews with the implementing organisation
Selected candidates are nominated by their Bundestag member
bundestag-ppp-2028-29.costs: Full scholarship from the German Bundestag.

bundeswettbewerb-mathematik-2027.about:
The Bundeswettbewerb Mathematik has three rounds. Rounds 1 and 2 each give four problems in geometry, combinatorics, number theory or algebra, solved at home over two to three months; round 3 is an hour-long colloquium with mathematicians. Group work (up to three people) is allowed in round 1 only.

You need three correct solutions to win a prize and qualify for round 2. Federal winners are admitted to the German National Academic Foundation (Studienstiftung). Solutions are submitted by post, handwritten or typed, in German.
bundeswettbewerb-mathematik-2027.eligibility: Students in any grade at a school in Germany leading to the Abitur, or at a German school abroad. Solutions in German.
how_to_apply: Download the round-1 problems from December 2026
Solve at least one problem (three for a prize)
Register online once your work is ready
Post your solutions before the early-March deadline

caamun-iv-2026.about:
CAAMUN IV revives the student-run Model UN of Colegio Anglo Americano in Cali after its last edition in 2020, under the theme 'Building peace, not waiting for it'.

The conference runs 9–11 December 2026 at Colegio Anglo Americano, Cali, Colombia. It is open to secondary school students. Working language: Spanish and English.

Register through the official site. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: Theme: 'Building peace, not waiting for it'
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
caamun-iv-2026.eligibility: Open to secondary school students. Working language: Spanish and English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Register through the official site.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
caamun-iv-2026.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

caltech-surf-2027.about:
SURF is Caltech's flagship undergraduate research programme: students work full-time for ten weeks on a project they design with a Caltech (or JPL) mentor, write a research proposal in advance, and finish with a technical paper and an oral presentation at SURF Seminar Day.

Non-Caltech students can apply if they are continuing undergraduates with at least a 2.5/4.0 GPA, and international students can take part on the Caltech campus (JPL placements are only for US citizens and permanent residents). The key step is finding a Caltech faculty mentor who agrees to host you and co-develop the proposal, so start contacting labs in winter. The 2027 stipend is USD 8,354 for ten weeks.
highlights: Design your own research project with a Caltech mentor
Open to non-Caltech and international undergraduates
caltech-surf-2027.eligibility: Continuing undergraduates in a degree programme, eligible to register in the autumn, with GPA ≥ 2.5/4.0 and at least two semesters (three quarters) completed. International students may participate on the Caltech campus; JPL projects are limited to US citizens/permanent residents.
how_to_apply: Identify Caltech faculty whose research interests you and email them about hosting you
Agree a project with a mentor and write a research proposal
Ask referees for letters
Submit the SURF application before the 2027 deadline (check the SURF Announcements of Opportunity and the SFP site)
If selected, arrange a visa and work authorisation
caltech-surf-2027.costs: Stipend USD 8,354 for ten weeks (2027). Housing is not automatically provided; plan for living costs in Pasadena.

canada-usa-mathcamp-2027.about:
Mathcamp is a five-week residential summer programme where about 120 students choose from dozens of university-level classes (combinatorics, topology, cryptography, analysis and more), work on projects, and live in a campus community with mathematicians. In 2026 it ran 28 June – 2 August at Champlain College, Burlington, Vermont; the 2027 location and dates are announced in December.

Admission is based mainly on the Qualifying Quiz, a set of challenging problems that you solve at home and submit with your application. There is no application fee. The base fee was USD 7,500 in 2026, but over USD 100,000 a year goes to need-based scholarships: international students can receive full scholarships and travel grants.
highlights: Students design their own timetable from dozens of advanced maths classes
Admission through a take-home Qualifying Quiz; no application fee
Full scholarships and travel grants available to international students
canada-usa-mathcamp-2027.eligibility: Mathematically talented students aged 13–18 from any country. Good English required. Admission is by application and the Qualifying Quiz.
how_to_apply: Sign up for the Mathcamp mailing list and check the site in December 2026 for 2027 dates
When the 2027 Qualifying Quiz is published, solve as many problems as you can and write full solutions
Fill in the online application (essay, recommendation) by the deadline (late February in 2026)
Apply for financial aid at the same time if needed
Decisions are announced in mid-April
canada-usa-mathcamp-2027.costs: 2026 base fee USD 7,500 covering tuition, room, board, activities and airport transfers; final fee after aid ranges from 0 to 7,500. No application fee. Need-based aid, full scholarships and travel grants available to international students.

canadian-team-mathematics-contest-2027.about:
The CTMC combines individual, team and relay rounds in a fun, fast-paced day of mathematics. Teams of six students from grades 9–12 compete; schools can enter one team in the Waterloo-hosted event (by lottery) or run unlimited teams in school.

The Waterloo event includes a campus experience; virtual participation is also possible.
canadian-team-mathematics-contest-2027.eligibility: Teams of six secondary-school students (grades 9–12) with one educator; in-school option open to schools in all regions.
how_to_apply: Teacher enters the UWaterloo lottery by 19 Nov 2026, or orders the in-school event by 12 Apr 2027
Form a team of six
Compete on 13 April (Waterloo) or from 14 April (in school)
canadian-team-mathematics-contest-2027.costs: CAD 240 per team in person / CAD 60 virtual at UWaterloo; in-school CAD 50 for unlimited teams plus processing.
